summary: Windows modules use the Ansible.Secrets C# util's SecretMasker with RegisterSecret (string or SecureString, preferred to avoid AMSI exposure) and MaskString, with a PowerShell example.
questions: How do I register a secret in a PowerShell module?
How do I mask a string before writing it to a file in a Windows module?
Why use the SecureString overload of RegisterSecret?

answer_card.title: Secret masking in PowerShell modules
answer_card.answer_md:
```powershell
#AnsibleRequires -CSharpUtil Ansible.Basic
#AnsibleRequires -CSharpUtil Ansible.Secrets
[Ansible.Secrets.SecretMasker]::RegisterSecret($session.Token)
$summary = [Ansible.Secrets.SecretMasker]::MaskString("Connected with token $($session.Token)")
```
- `RegisterSecret(string)` / `RegisterSecret(SecureString)`: prefer SecureString so plain text isn't exposed to AMSI.
- `MaskString(value[, placeholder])`.

`no_log` options are registered automatically.
